channel.title: The Boring Edit
channel.description: A quiet, personal, editorial blog by Nirmit Aggarwal — warm paper, ink text, one loud orange. Written in markdown, compiled to static ink.

item.title: Bash: Defensive Wizardry
item.description: Part 11 of the bash crash course: making scripts trustworthy — the four-letter ward set -euo pipefail, trap for cleanup magic, and bash -x for seeing what the spell actually casts.

item.title: Bash: Forks in the Road
item.description: Part 07 of the bash crash course: conditionals — if/elif/else, the test brackets and their gotchas, file existence checks, and case, the most readable spell in the book.

item.title: Bash: Jobs & Signals
item.description: Part 12 of the bash crash course: process control — background jobs with &, the Ctrl-Z suspend dance, fg/bg/jobs, kill and the signal ladder, nice, and nohup for spells that outlive their summoner.

item.title: Bash: Labelled Boxes
item.description: Part 06 of the bash crash course: variables and quoting rules (the #1 source of beginner bugs), command substitution, environment variables, and how $PATH decides which spells you can cast.

item.title: Bash: On Every Machine
item.description: Part 02 of the bash crash course: getting a real shell on Windows (Git Bash vs WSL), what macOS's zsh switch means, and the keyboard habits — Tab, Ctrl-R, history — that make you fast.

item.title: Bash: Pipes & Plumbing
item.description: Part 05 of the bash crash course: stdin, stdout, stderr — and how pipes and redirection turn twenty small commands into an infinite assembly line.

item.title: Bash: Text Alchemy
item.description: Part 10 of the bash crash course: the text-processing battery — sed find-and-replace, awk column surgery, cut, sort, uniq, tr — and the pipelines that glue them into one-liners of mass productivity.

item.title: Bash: The Custom Grimoire
item.description: Part 13 of the bash crash course: making everything permanent — the .bashrc file, aliases, functions you keep forever, and a two-line prompt upgrade that saves you ten questions a day.

item.title: Bash: The Hunters
item.description: Part 04 of the bash crash course: a deep dive into grep and find — searching text inside files and files inside machines — plus xargs, the spell that chains the hunt to the kill.

item.title: Bash: The Loop
item.description: Part 08 of the bash crash course: loops — for over globs and lists, while read over lines, C-style counting, break/continue, and the batch moves that turn an hour of clicking into one line.

item.title: Bash: The Prompt
item.description: Part 01 of a 15-part bash crash course: what a shell actually is, how to read the prompt, your first commands, and how to summon the ancient tome (the man page) when you forget the words.

item.title: Bash: The Quest Board
item.description: Part 15, the finale of the bash crash course: six complete capstone scripts — bulk renamer, rotating backup, site monitor, project scaffolder, disk hunter, and a terminal quiz game — each built from the previous fourteen parts.

item.title: Bash: The Spell Factory
item.description: Part 09 of the bash crash course: packaging logic into functions, feeding them arguments, returning codes instead of values, and the src-the-file trick that turns your terminal into a workshop.

item.title: Bash: The Spellbook
item.description: Part 03 of the bash crash course: the everyday file commands — ls, cd, cp, mv, rm and friends — plus glob wildcards, the closest thing computing has to actual magic.

item.title: Bash: The Wider Realm
item.description: Part 14 of the bash crash course: bash beyond your machine — SSH and keys, cron schedules, git hooks, and CI pipelines. The payoff chapter: why everything before this was worth it.

item.title: Rusty's Type
item.description: Part 03 of the Rust crash course: every primitive type (integers, floats, bool, char, tuples, arrays), variables and shadowing, constants vs statics, and custom types with structs and enums — with code and output at every step.

item.title: Hello, The Boring Edit
item.description: Welcome to The Boring Edit — a calm corner of the internet where I document what I'm learning, building, reading and thinking about. Here's what lives here and why it exists.

item.title: Introduction to Rust: why it exists, who runs on it, and how to start today
item.description: Why Rust exists, the memory problems it eliminates, which big organisations and projects run on it, how to install it in minutes, and the communities that support it.

item.title: Rusty's Hello World!
item.description: A detailed tour of Rust's printing macros — print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln!, write! and format! — plus the formatting engine: positional and named args, padding, radix, and Display vs Debug with code-output examples.
